scope: Proposition 6.15 (Universality of a fresh strip) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let C already satisfy the working package. In addition to its fixed template F, one may use a presentation G with the following properties: it has a fixed set of finite-support labels; every presentation G(J) used below, for an order of size µ, is an object of C at level µ; order embeddings give C-arrows; and the diagrams of its term lists are natural, including in the order enlargements and padded orders used. Assume also that these labels represent every element of G(J). Require µ to exceed the cardinality of the label set of G and to be closed under the bounds below with that cardinal included in their fixed input data. Put A = G(J). Insert into J a fresh convex strip of size µ with countably many disjoint convex substrips, each of size µ, and denote the resulting object by A+. Then every same-level extension of A embeds into A+ over A. In particular this applies to G = F and to well-ordered presentations. No separate union or categoricity assertion for a category of G-presentations is required.
